text: What is the requirement beyond simply having a base case?
choices: There must be exactly one base case
Every recursive call must move strictly closer to it, and it must be reachable from every accepted input
The recursion must be no more than ten deep
The base case must return zero
explanation: factorial(n) calling factorial(n) has a base case and never approaches it. This is Chapter 9's termination argument unchanged: n is a non-negative integer decreasing by one, so it cannot decrease forever.
